ultimately: says what finally happens after a long process or many events
typical: neutral to formal, before a verb or adjective, e.g. ultimately approved. NOT for: the last item in a list (use 'finally').
After years of debate, the council ultimately approved the plan.
The talks were tense but ultimately productive.
She tried several jobs and ultimately became a pilot.
introduces the most basic point that matters after everything else is considered
typical: at the start of a sentence, writing and careful speech. NOT for: describing a result in time.
Ultimately, it's your choice, not mine.
Ultimately, a good school depends on its teachers.
Ultimately, all we want is a safe place to live.
unless: says that something will happen or be true if something else does not happen
typical: unless = 'if ... not', e.g. Unless you hurry... NOT for: imagined past situations (use 'if ... had not').
Unless you tell me the password, I can't help you.
The shop won't open unless the manager arrives.
Don't call me before eight unless it's urgent.
use up: use all of something so that none is left
typical: use up the milk/your savings, use sth up. NOT for: using only a little.
Who used up all the hot water?
She used her savings up in six months.
usher in: mark the beginning of a new period or system
typical: usher in a new era/age/system. NOT for: ending something.
The invention ushered in a new age of travel.
The new president promised to usher in change.
show someone politely to a place
typical: usher sb in. NOT for: forcing someone to go.
A waiter ushered us in and gave us a table.
She ushered the guests in and offered them tea.
